product_principles: Recognize many kinds of contribution with a portfolio of leaderboards and evidence-backed contributor profiles; do not collapse them into a single winner score.
Raw activity, accepted deliverables, human stewardship and current project state are different lenses. Each must say what it measures.
Public source evidence and direct actor attribution come first. Unknown and unavailable are explicit states; missing history never becomes zero.
All contributors who make eligible public contributions can appear, including external contributors; organization membership is not eligibility.
Research merged means reviewed research, not production implementation, independent verification of every claim, or project completion.
Users can select category, repository, Project, workstream and window; profiles show breadth and accepted artifacts without requiring high code volume.
No leaderboard rewards line bloat, repeated toggles, issue churn, extra comments, favorable reviews, excessive hours, or private access.

organization_history_policy.repository_identity: Stable repository ID, with dated owner/name aliases and observed membership intervals.
organization_history_policy.default_scope: Organization contribution windows require evidence that the repository belonged to the organization at event time. Imported prior history can be shown in an explicitly separate inherited-history view.
rules: Repository created_at does not establish when it entered the organization; commit authored_at does not establish when it was integrated here.

For transferred repositories, record verified transfer/organization-adoption cutoff where available; if unavailable disclose unknown ownership boundary and exclude ambiguous old work from organization-specific comparisons.

A historical commit imported today remains historical author credit; the act of selecting/migrating it today can separately recognize import stewardship with evidence. Do not present old authored lines as newly written today.
Default-branch integration time for old commits may be unknown: preserve author/committer dates as those exact facts and avoid inventing an integration timestamp.
Forks, mirrors, transferred issues, squashed imports and cherry-picks require lineage records and reviewed dedupe decisions. Keep original author provenance when available.
Changes outside the org do not become organization contributions merely because an account later joins. External PR authors can qualify without membership.
Never fabricate manual-work volume from API operation count. Administrative batch setup is legitimate stewardship, grouped and labeled in its own category.
organization_history_policy.audit_evidence: source-audit.json and ../docs/SOURCE_AUDIT.md; the source snapshot is time-bounded.

identity.primary_key: GitHub node ID / numeric account ID; login is mutable display data
rules: Keep actor, subject, assignee, creator, pusher and committer distinct. Current assignees are ownership, not proof of completed work.
Use linked GitHub commit identities; do not expose emails or merge two people by display name.
Verified account migration/alias claims need proof and reversible, reviewed mapping.

Coauthor trailers provide attribution evidence, not fractional effort. Show shared artifacts. Fractional credit, if added, must be an explicitly named display allocation whose shares total one, never inferred effort.
Human activity can use automation; do not label an event AI-written from stylistic inference. Explicit contributor attestations are optional metadata.

Account actor is the provenance claim. A user account can operate through agents, scripts or batch CLI, so User type is not proof a human manually performed the work or authored the content. Never claim automatic detection of AI use.
Bots/system actors are a separate view. Combine __typename, account type, app identity and known automation actor registry; a single wasAutomated flag is insufficient.
Deleted/unavailable actors remain unknown/deleted, with preserved lawful aggregate lineage and no attempt at de-anonymization.

AI/model Co-authored-by trailers such as the audited Claude Opus 5.5 trailer are declared assistance metadata, not a human contributor identity. Preserve model name/version provenance without exposing trailer email addresses, inventing a GitHub user, or inferring unrecorded assistance.
A webhook sender can be the ghost placeholder or unresolved. Never attribute such events to a real named contributor; preserve unknown/system attribution and capability coverage.

privacy.default_scope: Allowlisted public repos and public artifacts only
rules: Do not require Members permission or expose private organization membership.
Do not collect private issues, private PRs, private Project notes, security alerts, interview identities, commit email addresses, hidden fields or tokens for a public leaderboard.
Treat a public Project containing inaccessible/private content as partial. Never publish its private item identifiers or infer hidden counts that disclose work.
On repository visibility change, transfer out, removal or installation suspension, quarantine affected public projections immediately pending scope revalidation.
Publish only sanitized metadata and deep links, not copied full comments/diffs by default.
Provide profile opt-out, display preferences, identity correction and data removal channels. Explain excluded/unknown coverage without naming opted-out people.
Counts already displayed may change after opt-out/deletion; version aggregates and do not preserve sensitive deleted text in correction logs.
Manual/external nominations must have contributor consent where needed and public evidence or an approved sanitized attestation.

classes.history: Supported source records can be backfilled subject to current access/deletion limits.
classes.history_partial: Some evidence is historical, but complete periods or subtypes require verification.
classes.observed: Reliably attributed only after collection starts; historical snapshots show state only.
classes.observed_partial: Observed event may lack counterpart identity or subtype coverage.
classes.snapshot: Current state at sample time, not authored change history.
classes.attested: Reviewed public evidence receipt required, not inferred automatically.
classes.attested_or_proven: Exact automated linkage or human-accepted receipt required.
classes.observed_or_attested: No reliable attribution from current state; observed actor event or receipt required.
classes.public_only: Only public and approved post-disclosure evidence can be included.
classes.disabled_currently: Feature disabled in audited repositories; not zero contribution.

rules: Backfill by repository objects and timeline/edit connections, not only organization Events API.
Never compare complete historical totals to observed-only totals without prominent coverage filtering.
Show zero only for a fully observed eligible scope and window with no events; otherwise show unavailable or partial.
A failed page, unsupported event type, partial GraphQL response or permission error prevents completeness certification.
Project current values, updatedAt, item creator, last editor or latest assignee cannot establish all intermediate changes.
UTC half-open intervals [start,end); viewer local formatting only; window comparison uses equal length and matched coverage.
Attribute accepted work to merge/acceptance date, opened work to created date, triage to actor event timestamp. Never substitute ingestion time for event time.
Retain occurred_at, source_created_at, source_updated_at, received_at, observed_at and effective_at separately.
Late delivery/backfill can revise a period; publish revision timestamp and stable receipt links.
No required streaks, weekend/hour counts or estimates of employee effort.
For new contributors show tenure cohorts only if opted for and labeled known first observed activity, not employment start.
Deduplicate webhook deliveries by installation + delivery GUID, and source entities/events by canonical node ID. Delivery ID alone is not semantic deduplication.
Join webhook, REST timeline, GraphQL timeline and edit history representations of the same underlying action; do not count four inputs as four actions.

If no authoritative event ID mapping exists, use conservative semantic matching with source object, action, actor, before/after, event time and relation identity; keep ambiguous collisions pending instead of guessing.
For relations normalize parent-child and blocking edge direction, dedupe mirrored endpoint events; relates-to is an unordered pair.
For triage recognition group related change bursts and count distinct meaningful items; keep raw audit counts separately.
Repository transfers/renames retain ID; object transfers require explicit alias lineage and verified mapping.
Same commit SHA seen in multiple mirrors or releases is not multiple organization accomplishments. Distinct repo edits are not deduped merely by similar title.
Initial imports, generated schemas, bulk migration/setup and mirrored history form a separate baseline lens; never silently label their size as new authored code.

Batch generation of a plan may create hundreds of valid issues and relations: retain raw actor events but group setup campaigns and use reviewed deliverable/outcome recognition rather than treating every new issue as equal merit.
Future leaderboard repository contributions qualify under same rules; generated snapshots, bot refresh commits and bulk initial import stay separate.
Default recognition uses public, attributable contributions satisfying the published per-metric policy.
Distinguish a first human contribution from automated application actions.
Separate submitted, merged/reviewed, verified/reproduced, and deployed stages.

Exclude synthetic fixtures, examples, generated artifacts, minified files, vendored code, lockfiles, package outputs and imported archives from eligible authored code LOC by default; show excluded amounts and classification reasons.
Research text, metadata and JSON proposals can be valuable contributions without being counted as software code.
Recognize removals, corrections and documented negative findings.
No numerical quality inference from LOC, comments, labels, raw citations, approval counts, stars, followers or reaction counts.
No automatic fraud penalty. Anomaly rules flag repeated toggles, mass duplicate filings, reciprocal low-value nominations and suspicious splits for review.
Store observed facts separately from eligibility decisions and recognition receipts. Version metric definitions, classifiers and policy.
A correction has ID, affected event/artifact/metric, reason, evidence, reviewer, effective date, status and superseding correction link.
Use reversible projection exclusions/adjustments; retain lawful minimal audit lineage without retaining redacted sensitive content.
Do not subtract reputation for reverted work. Historical merge remains factual; currently effective contribution can be separately filtered.
A reopened or duplicate-closed issue does not become multiple solved issues.
Contributors can dispute identity, categorization, missing events and nominations; moderators have conflict-of-interest and appeal rules.
Manual credits require public receipt, rationale and reviewer and must never masquerade as API observed facts.
Freeze award periods only with disclosed coverage and allow labeled corrections; profile rankings can change after backfill.

line_count_policy.definition: Eligible additions + deletions integrated into the default branch once, with PR lead and original contributor lineage as attribution facts, not exclusive personal authorship. Intermediate target-branch PR diffs remain a separately labeled raw view.
rules: Pin base/head/merge lineage and diff algorithm. Use final default-branch integration once; do not sum every intermediate push or stacked PR merge.
Show PR count by target branch and raw per-PR diff volume separately from repository default-branch delta. A merged PR into another feature branch is a merge fact, not delivered LOC.

The organization audit found 107 commit entries across merged research PRs but only 92 unique SHAs and 11 merges into intermediate branches: these are required deduplication fixtures, not independent delivered units.
Use .gitattributes and versioned path rules; classification overrides are reviewed and apply consistently across contributors.
Do not call net negative change poor contribution; do not rank by minified bytes or binary-size changes.
Renames/moves and formatting-only edits require classification; text additions/deletions from such changes are context only.
For multi-author/squashed PRs retain shared attribution and do not invent exact personal line ownership.
REST list PR files caps at 3000 files. If change exceeds cap or patches are truncated/omitted, use an isolated read-only Git diff at pinned refs or mark partial/unavailable.
Do not run checked-out repository code, hooks, filters or submodules when calculating diffs. Apply disk/time/memory bounds and no credential persistence in clone URLs.

Repository statistics are diagnostic cross-checks, not authoritative personal ledger: they aggregate differently and may omit merges/empty commits or return zero additions/deletions for large histories.
Prefer a small reviewed YAML/JSON record in leaderboard repo linked to source PR/issue; no new fields patched into imported v1 contracts.
Acceptance must verify evidence criteria; bot validation checks structure only.
Do not create a second research ownership system. Existing issue assignees and review authorities remain source of truth.
Nominations for external design, mentoring, outreach and sanitized operations work use the same public traceability rules.

architecture.recommended_shape: Small TypeScript modular service + PostgreSQL + queue/outbox + public web frontend, with durable data outside Git. Exact deployment vendor belongs in parent project decision. Avoid one cron job committing scoreboard JSON as the live source of truth.
pipeline: Validate HMAC over raw body and expected content/size, identify installation and allowlisted source, persist delivery transactionally, then acknowledge quickly.
Durable queue/outbox processes delivery idempotently; fetch authoritative objects as needed. Keep webhook event-time facts even if hydration current state is later.
Canonicalize actor, object, relation and time, link duplicate observations, attach coverage and scope.
Apply versioned classification/eligibility policies and receipts; do not modify upstream GitHub metadata.
Update per-window aggregates and contributor/artifact projections; only publish authorized public fields.
SSE/event invalidation refreshes clients using resumable sequence IDs; normal cached polling fallback; the user sees last updated and gaps.
Scheduled overlapping incremental scans reconcile source changes; periodic full count and pagination audits catch missed events.
Late events, corrections and policy changes rebuild affected periods deterministically without inventing event actors.
storage_security: Store only minimum needed source payload fields by default. If short-lived raw delivery quarantine is used, encrypt it, restrict access and expire it under a published retention policy.
Long-lived ledger stores public/minimized evidence and hashes, not full private raw payloads.
Secrets in managed secret store, scoped short-lived installation tokens and rotated webhook secrets; no credentials in browser or public build environment.
Untrusted titles, Markdown, URLs, filenames and diffs never execute. Escape rendering, sanitize URLs/Markdown, prevent formula injection in CSV exports and validate open redirects.
Outbound hydration targets GitHub API or approved static artifacts only; arbitrary user URL fetch requires SSRF protection and separate worker.
Public API cache keys include scope/definition version and cannot expose admin/private projections. Admin requires organization-approved authentication, authorization and audit.
Separate production/staging apps, databases and public hostnames. Canary/test events are marked synthetic and never contribute to real rankings.

suggested_slos.webhook_ack: Target p95 <2 seconds, always below GitHub 10-second timeout after durable acceptance.
suggested_slos.publication: Target p95 <60 seconds from received webhook to public projection under normal load; expose upstream/queue delays.
suggested_slos.reconciliation: Incremental every 5-15 minutes with overlap; daily completeness audit; exact intervals adapt to rate budget.
suggested_slos.recovery: App delivery polling within 3-day retention, outbox retries and replay; missed periods visibly partial until reconciled.
suggested_slos.availability: Define owner/cost/failure budget before launch, then test backup restore and read-only degraded mode.

sync_algorithm: Enumerate installation access + allowlisted public repos by ID. Inventory Projects and fields separately.
Backfill repository PRs/issues/commits/releases with explicit page exhaustion and source counts. No search-only enumeration, because search coverage/caps are unsuitable.
For every issue/PR paginate timeline, comments, review records, threads and userContentEdits independently; nested first:100 is not completeness.
Persist per-resource cursors and transactional watermarks only after successful page ingestion; restarted jobs must resume safely.
Incremental scans use overlapping updatedAt windows and periodic full sweeps. Timeline-specific events may require parent rescans even if parent updatedAt is unreliable.
Respect Retry-After/rate reset with jitter, per-installation concurrency/budget, exponential backoff, circuit breaker and dead letter queue; never busy-loop 403/429.
Distinguish 404 due to access/deletion from absence. Redaction/repository visibility checks run ahead of publishing.
Compare materialized counts/eligible event samples with raw evidence; GraphQL HTTP 200 can still carry errors/partial data.

rate_constraints.rest: Ordinary authenticated/App installation baseline 5000 requests/hour; enterprise/scaling differs. Read response rate headers; the runtime budget is authoritative.
rate_constraints.graphql: Ordinary user/App installation baseline 5000 points/hour with separate bucket and scaling; first/last 1..100; max 500000 requested nodes; split deep queries.
rate_constraints.secondary: Shared REST/GraphQL concurrency limits exist; use very low bounded concurrency and adaptive pacing, not maximum theoretical throughput. Honor 403/429 and error bodies.
